---
title: "Tech Value: fair price"
subtitle: "Which parts cost less, or more, than their benchmark performance predicts"
---

```{python}
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

# Bundle the table script into the page instead of loading it from a CDN.
init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

parts, meta = site.load("tech-value", "fair_price")
board, board_meta = site.load("tech-value", "fair_price_leaderboard")
verdicts = meta.get("verdicts") or {}
threshold = meta.get("gap_pct_threshold")
KINDS = {"gpu": "Graphics cards", "cpu": "Processors"}
```

A **fair price** is the price a part would have if price followed its
[Blender benchmark](https://opendata.blender.org/) score and nothing else. The **gap** is how
far the lowest listing is from that price: a negative gap means the part is cheap for the
rendering performance it delivers.

The fair price for a part always comes from a fit that never saw that part. Several models
compete, and a naive baseline (every part costs the same per point of score) is always on the
leaderboard. A model only replaces the baseline when it clearly beats it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
for kind, label in KINDS.items():
    v = verdicts.get(kind)
    if v:
        print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**{label}: does a model beat the baseline?** {v["statement"]}\n'
              f'{site.finding_line(v.get("finding"))}:::\n')
```

A gap is a question, not an answer. Blender measures rendering only. A processor built for
games, or a graphics card with more memory, can cost more than its rendering score predicts
and still be priced sensibly. Graphics cards also run on different Blender backends, which
favours NVIDIA, so AMD and Intel cards look expensive here for that reason alone.

```{python}
from pdi.tech_value import dashboard

READING_COLORS = {
    "below fair price": "#1baf7a",
    "near fair price": "#2a78d6",
    "above fair price": "#eb6834",
}


def section(kind: str):
    part = parts[parts["kind"] == kind].copy() if len(parts) else parts
    if part.empty:
        return Markdown(site.empty_state(meta, KINDS[kind]))
    part["display_model"] = part["model_key"].map(dashboard.display_name)
    fig = px.scatter(
        part, x="score", y="price_usd", color="reading", symbol="confidence",
        hover_name="display_model", log_x=True, log_y=True,
        color_discrete_map=READING_COLORS,
        hover_data={"fair_price_usd": ":.0f", "gap_pct": ":+.0f", "n_listings": True, "display_model": False},
        category_orders={"reading": ["below fair price", "near fair price", "above fair price"]},
        labels={"score": "Blender benchmark score (log scale)", "price_usd": "Lowest new listing, USD (log scale)",
                "reading": "Reading", "confidence": "Confidence", "fair_price_usd": "Fair price (USD)", "gap_pct": "Gap (%)"},
    )
    fig.update_traces(marker=dict(size=11, line=dict(width=1, color="rgba(255,255,255,0.6)")))
    line = part.sort_values("score")
    fig.add_scatter(x=line["score"], y=line["fair_price_usd"], mode="lines",
                    line=dict(dash="dash", width=2, color="#6c757d"), name="Fair price curve", hoverinfo="skip")
    fig.update_layout(
        height=440,
        margin=dict(t=24, r=20, b=52, l=64),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        yaxis=dict(tickprefix="$", separatethousands=True),
        xaxis=dict(separatethousands=True),
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="left", x=0),
    )
    fig.show()
    names = {m["id"]: m["name"] for m in meta.get("sources", [])}
    table = part.assign(
        model_key=part["display_model"],
        Cheapest=[
            f'<a href="{url}">{names.get(key, key)}</a>' if url else names.get(key, key)
            for key, url in zip(part["retailer"], part["listing_url"])
        ],
    )[["model_key", "gap_pct", "price_usd", "fair_price_usd", "reading", "confidence",
        "n_listings", "Cheapest"]].rename(columns={
        "model_key": "Model", "gap_pct": "Gap (%)", "price_usd": "Lowest price (USD)",
        "fair_price_usd": "Fair price (USD)", "reading": "Reading",
        "confidence": "Confidence", "n_listings": "Listings", "Cheapest": "Cheapest at",
    }).round({"Gap (%)": 0, "Fair price (USD)": 0})
    return show(table, paging=True, pageLength=25, order=[[1, "asc"]], showIndex=False,
                classes="display compact", allow_html=True)
```

## Graphics cards

```{python}
section("gpu")
```

## Processors

```{python}
section("cpu")
```

A part with a **single listing** is shown but was not used to fit the fair price. One listing
is often a marketplace seller's asking price for a part that is no longer made.

## Leaderboard

Error is measured by leaving each part out in turn and predicting its price from the others.

```{python}
if board.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(board_meta, "Fair price leaderboard")))
else:
    table = board.assign(kind=board["kind"].map(KINDS)).rename(columns={
        "kind": "Parts", "model": "Model", "n_parts": "Parts fitted",
        "mae_log": "Mean error (log)", "median_abs_pct_error": "Typical error (%)",
        "used": "Used", "is_baseline": "Baseline",
    }).round({"Mean error (log)": 3, "Typical error (%)": 1})
    show(table, paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```
